exposure: MCA/UA pulsatility index ratio (categorized as <=1 or >1)
cohort: The study included 200 pregnant women diagnosed with preeclampsia or gestational hypertension after 30 weeks of gestation.
finding: An abnormal MCA/UA pulsatility index ratio (<=1) is significantly associated with a higher incidence of severe oligohydramnios, emergency cesarean sections, low birth weight infants, and NICU admissions in women with preeclampsia and gestational hypertension.
mod_finding: Women with an abnormal MCA/UA ratio (<=1) had a significantly higher incidence of emergency cesarean sections (71.15%) compared to those with a ratio >1 (37.16%).
birth_weight: Babies with low birth weight (<2.5 kg) were identified as an outcome.
gest_age: Pregnant women included in the study were after 30 weeks of gestation.
